collection_batches.notes: Migrated the original statistical seed after removing three constructed methods without adequate primary-source support.
Filled missing statistical taxonomy cells using primary papers, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, statsmodels, and StatsForecast.
Collected distinct TSFM architectures and materially different releases; model sizes and checkpoint aliases were collapsed.
Collected ensembles, selectors, residual corrections, and fallbacks with explicit parent-method lineage.
Deepened neural, probabilistic, multivariate, reconciliation, robustness, calibration, volatility, and recent TSFM coverage.
Every named mechanism was already represented; wrappers, aliases, and parameterized variants were mapped to existing canonical cards.
Reviewed official benchmark integrations and model families; checkpoint sizes and release aliases did not introduce a new forecasting mechanism.
Added the zero-cost LLM model selector. AdapTS, AdaPTS, and SeqFusion were already represented.

assumptions: At least half of the component forecasts remain reasonably centered.
methods.description: Take the pointwise median of forecasts from heterogeneous component methods.
failure_conditions: A majority of similarly biased components moves the median in the wrong direction.

assumptions: Recent relative validation performance persists into the forecast window.
methods.description: Weight component forecasts inversely to their rolling-origin validation errors.
failure_conditions: Noisy short validation windows assign extreme weight to accidental winners.

assumptions: The estimated error covariance is stable and component forecasts are approximately unbiased.
methods.description: Estimate component error covariance and choose minimum-variance linear combination weights.
failure_conditions: Ill-conditioned covariance estimates produce unstable or extreme weights.

assumptions: Out-of-fold component error relationships transfer to the future window.
methods.description: Train a second-level regressor on out-of-fold component forecasts to produce the final forecast.
failure_conditions: Leakage or too few folds causes the meta-regressor to overfit component noise.

assumptions: Component quantiles share the same probability levels and are individually ordered.
methods.description: Average corresponding predictive quantiles from multiple probabilistic forecasters.
failure_conditions: Miscalibrated or dependent components can preserve bias and yield incoherent quantile curves.

assumptions: Historical forecast-origin errors rank candidate methods similarly to the next origin.
methods.description: Select the single component with the lowest rolling-origin validation loss for the target horizon.
failure_conditions: A regime change after the last validation origin makes the historical champion obsolete.

assumptions: A representative reference collection links series features to relative model performance.
methods.description: Map time-series features to learned nonnegative weights over a pool of forecasting methods.
failure_conditions: Targets outside the reference feature distribution receive unreliable weights.

assumptions: Enough historical origins exist to estimate horizon-specific error rankings.
methods.description: Choose a potentially different validated component for each forecast horizon step.
failure_conditions: Sparse long-horizon validation creates a jagged and unstable sequence of selections.

assumptions: Observable history features identify which expert is reliable for each target.
methods.description: Use a learned gating model to assign target-dependent weights to statistical and foundation forecasters.
failure_conditions: The gate overfits a small task collection or ignores a new failure mode shared by all experts.

assumptions: The series contains separable linear and nonlinear components.
methods.description: Forecast a linear ARIMA component and add a neural forecast fitted to its residual structure.
failure_conditions: Residual dependence changes after fitting or both components model the same signal twice.

assumptions: Systematic residual autocorrelation remains after the foundation forecast.
methods.description: Use TimesFM as the primary path and add an ARIMA forecast of historical primary-model residuals.
failure_conditions: Residuals estimated from too few pseudo-origins are noisy or change regime at deployment.

assumptions: Residual bias is predictable from historical, calendar, or known-future features.
methods.description: Add a lag-feature gradient-boosting correction trained on pseudo-out-of-sample Chronos residuals.
failure_conditions: In-sample residual leakage or unseen covariate states causes an oversized correction.

assumptions: ETS captures structural components while remaining residual dependence is linear and stable.
methods.description: Forecast level, trend, and seasonality with ETS, then add an autoregressive residual forecast.
failure_conditions: Residual correction double-counts seasonal dynamics or amplifies a structural break.

assumptions: History-only validation can detect harmful foundation-model mismatch before deployment.
methods.description: Use a foundation forecast only when it clears a margin over a statistical challenger in rolling validation.
failure_conditions: A future event changes the regime in a way no historical fold can reveal.

assumptions: Pretraining is more reliable than local estimation only in the short-history regime.
methods.description: Use a zero-shot foundation model below a data threshold and switch to a fitted statistical model once history is sufficient.
failure_conditions: The threshold is poorly calibrated or the foundation model is mismatched to the target domain.

assumptions: The anomaly diagnostic separates contamination from genuine persistent changes.
methods.description: Choose a robust or intervention-adjusted forecaster when anomaly diagnostics exceed a threshold, otherwise use the primary model.
failure_conditions: A true regime shift is labeled as an outlier and routed to an inappropriate robust fallback.

assumptions: Fallback parents are valid substitutes and operational failures are detected before emitting a forecast.
methods.description: Execute an ordered list of forecasters and fall back when a model cannot satisfy context, covariate, device, or runtime constraints.
failure_conditions: Silent model degradation passes the availability checks and prevents fallback activation.

assumptions: Combined forecast errors have stable serial dependence observable at the next forecast origin.
methods.description: Correct a combined forecast by adding an estimated predictable fraction of the preceding combined forecast error.
failure_conditions: Changing error dependence or delayed labels makes the correction stale or unavailable.

assumptions: A representative reference collection maps time-series features to future method performance.
methods.description: Predict each candidate model's forecast error from series features using Bayesian multivariate surface regression, then select or combine predicted winners.
failure_conditions: Targets outside the reference feature distribution receive misleading predicted errors.

assumptions: Model preference embeddings learned on representative tasks transfer to unseen forecasting configurations.
methods.description: Embed forecasting tasks and pretrained forecasters in a shared space, then select or ensemble the nearest model representations for a new series.
failure_conditions: A target outside the co-embedding reference distribution or a newly added uncharacterized model yields an unreliable ranking.

assumptions: Recent labeled feedback identifies the current distribution and relative value of the local and foundation forecasts.
methods.description: Learn a lightweight online forecaster from newly arriving observations and dynamically weight it with a frozen foundation-model forecast.
failure_conditions: Delayed feedback or fast alternating regimes make the online forecaster and weighting rule lag the target.

assumptions: A learnable feature-space transformation exposes dimensions that the univariate foundation model can forecast independently.
methods.description: Project a multivariate series into a latent space, apply a frozen univariate foundation model dimension-wise, and reconstruct a probabilistic multivariate forecast.
failure_conditions: The latent transformation cannot preserve changing cross-variate dependence or uncertainty under a new regime.

assumptions: Representation distance identifies complementary pretrained models whose sequential forecasts improve the target.
methods.description: Select pretrained forecasters by target-to-model representation distance, run them sequentially, and fuse their predictions with minimal target data.
failure_conditions: A poor shared representation or correlated model errors selects redundant forecasters and compounds bias.

assumptions: The language model can map a sufficiently informative series description to method capabilities and failure modes.
methods.description: Prompt a language model with time-series characteristics and candidate-method descriptions to select a forecaster without constructing a historical performance matrix.
failure_conditions: Weak numerical descriptions, unsupported candidate methods, or memorized popularity biases produce unreliable selections.

assumptions: assumes the most recent value is the best available estimate of near-future values
assumes no reliable trend or seasonal signal
methods.description: Repeats the last observed value for every future step (random walk without drift).
failure_conditions: degrades sharply when the series has a persistent trend
ignores seasonality entirely and fails on strongly seasonal series

assumptions: assumes the series is stationary around a constant mean
methods.description: Forecasts every future step as the historical mean of the series.
failure_conditions: fails on trending series
fails on seasonal series

assumptions: assumes the average historical rate of change continues unchanged
requires at least 2 observations
methods.description: Extrapolates a straight line from the first to the last observed value (random walk with drift).
failure_conditions: fails when the trend reverses direction after the observed window
amplifies noise from a volatile first or last observation

assumptions: requires a known seasonal_period and at least one full cycle of history
assumes the seasonal pattern is stable
methods.description: Repeats the value observed one full seasonal cycle ago for each future step.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than one seasonal cycle
fails on series without genuine periodicity
ignores any trend

assumptions: assumes local stationarity over the averaging window
requires history length >= window size
methods.description: Forecasts every future step as the mean of the last k observed values.
failure_conditions: lags behind trends by roughly half the window width
fails when history is shorter than the window

assumptions: assumes no trend and no seasonality
assumes an optimal smoothing parameter can be fit from history
methods.description: Simple exponential smoothing; forecasts a flat line at the smoothed level, weighting recent observations more heavily.
failure_conditions: systematically under- or over-shoots trending series
fails on seasonal series

assumptions: assumes an approximately linear trend with no seasonality
methods.description: Holt's linear (double) exponential smoothing; extrapolates a smoothed level and trend.
failure_conditions: over-extrapolates trend on long horizons
fails on seasonal series

assumptions: assumes a trend that weakens over time rather than continuing linearly
methods.description: Holt's linear trend with a damping parameter that flattens the trend over the forecast horizon.
failure_conditions: under-forecasts series with a genuinely persistent linear trend
fails on seasonal series

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes seasonal amplitude is roughly constant in absolute terms
methods.description: Holt-Winters triple exponential smoothing with additive seasonality.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
misfits series where seasonal amplitude scales with the level

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
requires strictly positive values
assumes seasonal amplitude scales with the level
methods.description: Holt-Winters triple exponential smoothing with multiplicative seasonality.
failure_conditions: undefined or unstable for series containing zero or negative values
fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes trend weakens over the forecast horizon
methods.description: Holt-Winters triple exponential smoothing with a damped trend component.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
under-forecasts series with a persistent linear trend

assumptions: assumes one of the standard ETS error-trend-season combinations reasonably fits the series
methods.description: Automatic selection among the additive/multiplicative/damped error-trend-season exponential smoothing state-space models by in-sample information criterion.
failure_conditions: selection can overfit short histories
multiplicative variants require strictly positive values

assumptions: assumes the series is well described by a linear trend and a locally weighted SES component
methods.description: Classical Theta method; decomposes the series into long-term trend and local-curvature theta-lines and recombines their forecasts.
failure_conditions: fails on strongly seasonal series without prior deseasonalization
degrades on very short histories

assumptions: assumes the classical Theta method's structure holds but with data-driven parameters
methods.description: Dynamic optimized Theta method; fits theta-line weights and smoothing parameters from history instead of using fixed defaults.
failure_conditions: can overfit very short histories
fails on strongly seasonal series without prior deseasonalization

assumptions: assumes the (differenced) series is stationary
assumes a linear autoregressive relationship
methods.description: Autoregressive model; forecasts each value as a linear combination of a fitted number of past values.
failure_conditions: fails on non-stationary series without differencing
fails on series dominated by seasonality

assumptions: assumes the (differenced) series is stationary
assumes shocks have a linear, short-memory effect
methods.description: Moving-average model; forecasts each value as a linear combination of past forecast errors.
failure_conditions: fails on non-stationary series without differencing
forecasts revert to the mean quickly and undershoot persistent trends

assumptions: assumes the series is stationary
assumes no seasonality
methods.description: Combined autoregressive moving-average model.
failure_conditions: fails on non-stationary or seasonal series without preprocessing

assumptions: assumes differencing to a low order achieves stationarity
assumes no seasonality
methods.description: Non-seasonal ARIMA with automatic (p, d, q) order selection by information criterion.
failure_conditions: order search can overfit short histories
fails on strongly seasonal series

assumptions: requires a known seasonal_period
requires enough history to estimate seasonal differencing reliably (multiple full cycles)
methods.description: Seasonal ARIMA with automatic (p, d, q)(P, D, Q, m) order selection by information criterion.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than a few seasonal cycles
order search can be unstable on noisy series

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes the seasonal component is stable
methods.description: STL-decomposes the series into trend, season, and remainder, extrapolates trend with a naive/drift method, and reapplies the last seasonal cycle.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
ignores structure in the remainder component

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes a fixed, non-evolving seasonal pattern
methods.description: Classical additive/multiplicative decomposition into trend, season, and remainder, recombined with a simple trend extrapolation.
failure_conditions: moving-average trend estimate loses the most recent seasonal cycles at the series edges
fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
methods.description: STL-decomposes the series, forecasts the seasonally adjusted series with ETS, and reapplies the seasonal component.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
compounds any ETS misfit from the decomposition step

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes the seasonally adjusted series is well modeled by ARIMA
methods.description: STL-decomposes the series, forecasts the seasonally adjusted series with ARIMA, and reapplies the seasonal component.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
compounds any ARIMA misfit from the decomposition step

assumptions: assumes the series is intermittent with a meaningful fraction of exact zeros
methods.description: Croston's method; separately smooths non-zero demand sizes and inter-demand intervals for sparse/intermittent series.
failure_conditions: produces a biased (upward) forecast, a known property of standard Croston
degrades on dense, non-intermittent series

assumptions: assumes the series is intermittent with a meaningful fraction of exact zeros
methods.description: Croston's method with the Syntetos-Boylan Approximation bias correction applied to the demand-size/interval smoothing.
failure_conditions: still assumes a stable demand-generating process
degrades on dense, non-intermittent series

assumptions: assumes the series is intermittent with a meaningful fraction of exact zeros
methods.description: Teunter-Syntetos-Babai method; smooths demand probability and size separately, allowing the forecast to decay during long zero runs.
failure_conditions: degrades on dense, non-intermittent series
sensitive to the choice of smoothing parameters on short histories

assumptions: assumes the series is intermittent
requires enough history to support the chosen aggregation level
methods.description: Aggregate-Disaggregate Intermittent Demand Approach; temporally aggregates the series to a lower-intermittence frequency, forecasts, then disaggregates.
failure_conditions: fails when history is too short for the aggregation level chosen
disaggregation can misallocate volume within an aggregated period

assumptions: assumes the series is intermittent
requires enough history to support multiple aggregation levels
methods.description: Multiple Aggregation Prediction Algorithm; combines forecasts across several temporal aggregation levels of an intermittent series.
failure_conditions: fails when history is too short for the coarsest aggregation level
more computationally expensive than single-level ADIDA for uncertain benefit

assumptions: assumes no trend or seasonality, only a slowly drifting level plus noise
methods.description: State-space local level (random walk plus noise) model estimated via the Kalman filter.
failure_conditions: fails on trending or seasonal series
underperforms simple naive methods when the level is actually constant

assumptions: assumes no seasonality, only a slowly evolving level and trend
methods.description: State-space local linear trend model (stochastic level and slope) estimated via the Kalman filter.
failure_conditions: fails on seasonal series
can produce unstable long-horizon trend extrapolation if slope variance is large

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history to estimate the seasonal state
methods.description: Basic structural model combining stochastic level, trend, and seasonal components in a single state-space model.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
estimation can be unstable on short or noisy series

assumptions: assumes the underlying trend is smooth and outliers are a minority of points
methods.description: Extrapolates a robust locally weighted (LOESS) trend fit, downweighting outliers.
failure_conditions: ignores seasonality entirely
extrapolation beyond the fitted window is unstable for highly nonlinear local trends

assumptions: assumes a small number of dominant, stable periodic frequencies
requires a known or estimable seasonal_period
methods.description: Regresses the series on a trend plus a fixed set of Fourier (sine/cosine) terms and extrapolates.
failure_conditions: fails on series with evolving or non-stationary periodicity
underfits series with sharp, non-sinusoidal seasonal shape

assumptions: assumes the trend is approximately linear
assumes no seasonality
methods.description: Ordinary least squares regression of the series on a linear time index, extrapolated forward.
failure_conditions: fails on seasonal or nonlinear-trend series
sensitive to outliers near the end of history

assumptions: assumes the trend is well approximated by a low-order polynomial
assumes no seasonality
methods.description: Least squares regression of the series on a low-order polynomial time index, extrapolated forward.
failure_conditions: extrapolation diverges quickly on longer horizons for polynomial order above 1
overfits short histories at higher polynomial orders

assumptions: assumes trend changes are sparse and detectable from history alone
assumes no seasonality
methods.description: Fits a piecewise linear trend with one or more detected changepoints and extrapolates the final segment.
failure_conditions: changepoint detection is unreliable on short or noisy histories
extrapolating the final segment assumes no imminent further change

assumptions: requires at least 2 full seasonal cycles of history
assumes blocks of history are representative of future dynamics
methods.description: Generates a forecast by block-bootstrapping historical seasonal-cycle-length blocks of the detrended series and averaging simulated paths.
failure_conditions: fails when history is shorter than 2 seasonal cycles
point forecast can be a poorly representative average when the simulated paths are multimodal

assumptions: assumes the three component methods have roughly independent errors so averaging reduces variance
methods.description: Averages the point forecasts of ets_auto, arima_auto, and theta_optimized.
failure_conditions: inherits any failure shared by all three components, e.g. all three fail on a very short or heavily intermittent series
requires all three component methods to be available

assumptions: Past states close in lag space have similar future continuations.
methods.description: Match the latest lag vector to historical lag vectors and average their observed continuations.
failure_conditions: Sparse history or a regime shift leaves no genuinely comparable analogue.

assumptions: Shape-similar episodes remain predictive despite local timing distortions.
methods.description: Find historical subsequences with similar shape under dynamic time warping and aggregate their following paths.
failure_conditions: A permissive warping window can match unrelated episodes and erase timing information.

assumptions: Calibration and forecast residuals are sufficiently exchangeable over the evaluation period.
methods.description: Calibrate forecast intervals with held-out absolute residual quantiles from a fixed point forecaster.
failure_conditions: Abrupt distribution shifts invalidate residual coverage learned from the calibration window.

assumptions: Coverage drift is gradual enough for online score updates to track it.
methods.description: Update conformal interval widths online so recent coverage errors change the next interval.
failure_conditions: Fast alternating regimes cause the adaptation rule to lag or oscillate.

assumptions: Conditional count variance is close to the conditional mean after included predictors.
methods.description: Model a count target with a log-linked Poisson mean driven by time and optional predictors.
failure_conditions: Strong overdispersion, zero inflation, or dependence left in residuals biases uncertainty.

assumptions: A negative-binomial conditional law captures extra-Poisson dispersion.
methods.description: Forecast overdispersed counts with a dynamic negative-binomial regression mean.
failure_conditions: Structural zeros or changing dispersion violate the fitted conditional distribution.

assumptions: Count dependence can be represented by stable thinning probabilities and innovations.
methods.description: Use binomial thinning of past integer counts plus an integer-valued innovation process.
failure_conditions: Nonlinear regime changes or strong covariate effects are not represented by a fixed INAR law.

assumptions: The chosen kernel expresses the smoothness and similarity structure of the lag-response map.
methods.description: Place a Gaussian-process prior over the nonlinear mapping from lag vectors to future values.
failure_conditions: Poor kernels extrapolate badly and exact inference scales cubically with training cases.

assumptions: A fixed kernel can represent the stable nonlinear relationship between features and target.
methods.description: Fit epsilon-insensitive support-vector regression to lag and calendar features and roll it forward.
failure_conditions: Recursive multi-step use compounds error and kernel tuning can be unstable on short series.

assumptions: Future responses vary smoothly under the selected kernel geometry.
methods.description: Apply ridge-regularized kernel regression to lagged and optional exogenous features.
failure_conditions: Kernel matrices become costly on large samples and extrapolation beyond observed features is weak.

assumptions: A stable nonlinear lag relationship can be learned from enough repeated patterns.
methods.description: Feed lagged observations and seasonal lags to a shallow multilayer perceptron and recursively forecast.
failure_conditions: Small samples, regime shifts, and recursive error accumulation degrade long-horizon forecasts.

assumptions: Related training series share learnable dynamics and the chosen likelihood is suitable.
methods.description: Train one autoregressive recurrent network across related series to output a parametric predictive distribution.
failure_conditions: Few unrelated series or a misspecified likelihood prevent useful global transfer.

assumptions: A large collection of training windows supports learning reusable basis expansions.
methods.description: Stack backward and forward fully connected residual blocks with optional trend and seasonal bases.
failure_conditions: Very small samples or abrupt unseen regimes cause high-variance extrapolation.

assumptions: Forecast structure can be decomposed across multiple temporal resolutions.
methods.description: Use hierarchical interpolation and multi-rate input pooling to model different forecast frequencies.
failure_conditions: Resolution choices can suppress sharp high-frequency events important to the target.

assumptions: Known-future and observed covariates contain stable cross-series predictive information.
methods.description: Combine recurrent local processing, variable selection, gating, and attention for multi-horizon forecasts with covariates.
failure_conditions: Sparse data or unreliable future covariates make the high-capacity architecture overfit.

assumptions: Outlier timing or intervention shape can be identified separately from recurring dynamics.
methods.description: Jointly estimate ARIMA dynamics and explicit pulse, level-shift, or temporary-change intervention effects.
failure_conditions: Many overlapping anomalies are confounded with structural breaks and ARIMA parameters.

assumptions: A sparse set of abnormal observations contaminates an otherwise stable ARIMA process.
methods.description: Detect additive and innovative outliers, estimate their effects, clean the series, and refit ARIMA.
failure_conditions: Persistent regime changes are incorrectly removed as isolated contamination.

assumptions: A small set of persistent latent regimes generates the observed dynamics.
methods.description: Use a latent Markov state to switch autoregressive parameters, level, or variance across regimes.
failure_conditions: Regimes with few visits are weakly identified and unprecedented states cannot be represented.

assumptions: Regime transitions are driven by observable threshold conditions.
methods.description: Switch autoregressive equations when a threshold variable crosses estimated cut points.
failure_conditions: Smooth transitions or time-varying thresholds make hard partitions unstable.

assumptions: Nonlinear dynamics vary smoothly with an observable transition variable.
methods.description: Blend autoregressive regimes continuously with a logistic or exponential transition function.
failure_conditions: Limited observations near the transition region make slope and threshold estimates unstable.

assumptions: Transformed seasonal dynamics and residual autocorrelation remain stable.
methods.description: Combine Box-Cox transformation, ARMA errors, trend, and one seasonal component in state space.
failure_conditions: Multiple or rapidly changing seasonalities are not captured by a single seasonal state.

assumptions: Complex seasonalities can be represented by stable Fourier state components.
methods.description: Extend BATS with trigonometric states so multiple and non-integer seasonal periods can be modeled.
failure_conditions: Long histories and many harmonics make fitting expensive and can overfit weak cycles.

assumptions: Seasonal shapes are smooth and repeat while residual autocorrelation follows ARIMA dynamics.
methods.description: Regress on Fourier terms for one or more seasonal periods while modeling remaining errors with ARIMA.
failure_conditions: Changing seasonal timing or event-driven pulses cannot be represented by fixed harmonics.

assumptions: Several stable seasonal periods coexist and can be separated additively.
methods.description: Decompose multiple seasonal periods with repeated STL, forecast the adjusted series with ETS, and restore each seasonal component.
failure_conditions: Short histories or interacting seasonal amplitudes make the sequential decomposition unreliable.

assumptions: Historical feature-target relationships recur within the range covered by training data.
methods.description: Train an ensemble of randomized regression trees on lag, rolling, calendar, and optional exogenous features.
failure_conditions: Trees do not extrapolate trends beyond observed target regions and recursive forecasts compound errors.

assumptions: Engineered features expose repeatable nonlinear splits predictive of future targets.
methods.description: Boost regularized regression trees over lag, rolling, calendar, and exogenous features.
failure_conditions: Extrapolation and unseen regimes remain weak even when in-range fit is strong.

assumptions: Large enough supervised windows support stable nonlinear partitions of engineered features.
methods.description: Fit histogram-based leaf-wise gradient-boosted trees to time-series lag and covariate features.
failure_conditions: Leaf-wise growth overfits small series and cannot reliably extrapolate outside training targets.

assumptions: Abrupt changes reset locally stable predictive parameters with a meaningful hazard prior.
methods.description: Maintain a posterior over the current run length and forecast from the regime implied by that posterior.
failure_conditions: Gradual drift or a misspecified hazard spreads posterior mass across misleading run lengths.

assumptions: The most recent detected segment is long enough and more relevant than older regimes.
methods.description: Use PELT to locate an optimal penalized segmentation and fit the forecasting model only to the latest regime.
failure_conditions: Penalty errors create a tiny final segment or retain obsolete observations after a missed break.

assumptions: A small fraction of observations are contaminated while trend and seasonality remain locally smooth.
methods.description: Apply robust STL weights, forecast the seasonally adjusted component with ETS, and restore seasonality.
failure_conditions: Persistent level shifts are downweighted as outliers instead of becoming the new forecast regime.

assumptions: Seasonal phase is stable and fewer than half of comparable cycles are contaminated.
methods.description: Estimate each seasonal position by a median across cycles and extrapolate the robust profile around a recent median level.
failure_conditions: Changing seasonal amplitude or phase makes the historical median profile obsolete.

assumptions: A small set of harmonic frequencies explains recurring behavior while amplitudes change gradually.
methods.description: Represent periodic behavior with stochastic trigonometric state pairs whose amplitudes evolve through a state-space model.
failure_conditions: Irregular event timing or rapidly changing frequencies cannot be tracked by fixed harmonic states.

assumptions: Conditional quantiles are stable functions of the supplied predictors.
methods.description: Fit separate conditional quantile regressions over lagged, calendar, and optional exogenous predictors.
failure_conditions: Sparse tail observations and independently fitted levels can produce unstable or crossing quantiles.

assumptions: Residual blocks approximate the dependence and scale of future forecast errors.
methods.description: Simulate future paths by adding resampled historical forecast residuals to recursive point forecasts.
failure_conditions: Heteroscedasticity or regime change makes historical residual draws miscalibrated.

assumptions: Bottom-level forecasts are reliable enough to determine every aggregate.
methods.description: Forecast the bottom-level series and aggregate them through the hierarchy summing matrix.
failure_conditions: Noisy disaggregated series propagate high variance into all upper levels.

assumptions: Historical component shares persist through the forecast horizon.
methods.description: Forecast the total and disaggregate it using proportions estimated from historical observations.
failure_conditions: Structural share shifts allocate an accurate total to the wrong bottom series.

assumptions: Relative base forecasts contain useful allocation information even when they are incoherent.
methods.description: Disaggregate an aggregate forecast using proportions derived from independently generated base forecasts.
failure_conditions: Biased or near-zero component base forecasts create unstable proportions.

assumptions: The chosen middle level balances signal strength and allocation stability.
methods.description: Forecast a selected middle level, aggregate upward, and disaggregate downward with estimated proportions.
failure_conditions: A poor middle-level choice inherits both noisy forecasts and unstable disaggregation.

assumptions: Base forecast errors have comparable, uncorrelated variance after scaling.
methods.description: Project incoherent base forecasts onto the coherent subspace using ordinary least squares.
failure_conditions: Strongly unequal or correlated errors make the unweighted projection inefficient.

assumptions: Diagonal weights capture the dominant reliability differences across nodes.
methods.description: Reconcile base forecasts with diagonal weights derived from hierarchy structure or forecast-error variances.
failure_conditions: Ignoring cross-series error covariance loses important offsetting information.

assumptions: Historical base forecast errors estimate future cross-series dependence after regularization.
methods.description: Use a shrinkage estimate of the full base-error covariance in minimum-trace forecast reconciliation.
failure_conditions: Few origins or changing dependence make even the shrunk covariance misleading.

assumptions: Different temporal scales offer complementary information and share stable aggregation constraints.
methods.description: Forecast multiple non-overlapping temporal aggregation levels and reconcile them to one coherent path.
failure_conditions: Misaligned calendars or scale-specific structural breaks invalidate the temporal hierarchy.

assumptions: A fixed linear projection of decomposed history captures the target horizon.
methods.description: Decompose the input into trend and remainder and map each component directly to the forecast with linear layers.
failure_conditions: Nonlinear conditional dynamics or new regimes cannot be represented by the fixed projection.

assumptions: A small set of dominant attention interactions captures long-range dependencies.
methods.description: Use ProbSparse attention, attention distillation, and a one-shot generative decoder for long-sequence forecasting.
failure_conditions: Diffuse dependencies or limited training data make sparse attention discard useful signals.

assumptions: Periodic sub-series dependencies and decomposable trend-seasonal structure persist.
methods.description: Embed progressive decomposition and sub-series auto-correlation blocks inside a Transformer architecture.
failure_conditions: Event-driven or aperiodic dynamics undermine auto-correlation aggregation.

assumptions: The target has a compact frequency-domain representation transferable across windows.
methods.description: Combine seasonal-trend decomposition with sparse Fourier or wavelet-domain Transformer operations.
failure_conditions: Sharp transient events spread energy across frequencies and are poorly reconstructed from sparse modes.

assumptions: Local patch structure transfers and channel independence does not discard essential interactions.
methods.description: Tokenize each variable into temporal patches and apply a channel-independent Transformer across patches.
failure_conditions: Strong cross-variable causal structure or badly chosen patch sizes reduces accuracy.

assumptions: Cross-variable relationships are stable and full-history variable embeddings preserve predictive temporal information.
methods.description: Invert standard tokenization so complete variable histories become tokens and attention models cross-variate relations.
failure_conditions: Very many variables or unstable cross-series relations make variate attention expensive or misleading.

assumptions: A small number of discoverable periods organizes intra-period and inter-period variation.
methods.description: Reshape one-dimensional histories into multiple period-aligned two-dimensional tensors and model them with inception blocks.
failure_conditions: Weak or drifting periodicity yields unstable two-dimensional reshaping.

assumptions: Time and feature mixing through dense projections captures the relevant multivariate dynamics.
methods.description: Stack MLP blocks that alternately mix information across time and feature dimensions.
failure_conditions: Long irregular dependencies or small training sets make dense mixers overfit.

assumptions: Dense nonlinear feature maps and known covariates are sufficient without explicit attention.
methods.description: Encode history and covariates with residual MLP blocks and decode the full long-horizon forecast directly.
failure_conditions: Unobserved long-range dependencies or unreliable future covariates produce systematic errors.

assumptions: Downsampled subsequences preserve complementary temporal relations at multiple resolutions.
methods.description: Recursively downsample the sequence, convolve each subsequence, and exchange information across resolutions.
failure_conditions: Aliasing or irregular sampling breaks the interleaved multi-resolution representation.

assumptions: Fine and coarse sampling scales contain complementary stable patterns.
methods.description: Decompose multi-scale histories, mix seasonal and trend information across scales, and combine scale-specific predictors.
failure_conditions: Scale construction smears sharp events or aliases irregular cycles.

assumptions: Flat-minimum optimization improves generalization of a compact cross-channel attention model.
methods.description: Train a shallow channel-attention Transformer with sharpness-aware minimization for multivariate forecasting.
failure_conditions: Optimization cost or unstable channel relations remove the expected generalization benefit.

assumptions: Complex-valued smoothing states capture stable oscillatory level and trend dynamics.
methods.description: Automatically select and fit a complex exponential smoothing model using information-criterion search.
failure_conditions: Irregular shocks or weak oscillation make the selected complex state unstable or unnecessary.

assumptions: Additive boosted components capture stable trend and multiple seasonal structures.
methods.description: Automatically combine multiple seasonalities, trend, and exogenous effects through MFLES boosting components.
failure_conditions: Abrupt regimes or poorly specified seasonal periods cause component leakage and overfit.

assumptions: Local changes in level and curvature can be tracked by dynamically updated Theta components.
methods.description: Allow the Theta model's decomposition and smoothing behavior to adapt dynamically rather than using fixed theta lines.
failure_conditions: Rapid structural breaks or short histories make the dynamic parameters unstable.

assumptions: Optimized smoothing parameters transfer to future intermittent arrivals and sizes.
methods.description: Estimate Croston demand-size and inter-arrival smoothing parameters by optimizing in-sample fit.
failure_conditions: Sparse observations make optimization noisy and obsolescence violates stationary arrival assumptions.

assumptions: Seasonal phase persists and recent matching cycles have a stable mean.
methods.description: Forecast each seasonal position with the average of its most recent matching seasonal observations.
failure_conditions: Level shifts or changing seasonal amplitude bias the fixed seasonal window average.

assumptions: Volatility clustering is driven by a stable finite history of squared shocks.
methods.description: Forecast conditional variance as a function of lagged squared innovations in an ARCH model.
failure_conditions: Long-memory or asymmetric volatility requires richer variance dynamics.

assumptions: A stable GARCH recursion captures persistent volatility clustering.
methods.description: Recursively forecast conditional variance from lagged squared innovations and lagged conditional variances.
failure_conditions: Leverage effects, structural breaks, or near-integrated variance make symmetric GARCH unreliable.

assumptions: Cross-series lag relationships are linear, stable, and estimable from sufficient history.
methods.description: Jointly forecast multiple stationary series using linear equations over lags of every variable.
failure_conditions: Many variables and lags exhaust sample size or structural changes invalidate coefficients.

assumptions: A stable cointegration rank and long-run equilibrium connect the component series.
methods.description: Combine short-run vector autoregression with error-correction terms for cointegrated nonstationary series.
failure_conditions: Rank misspecification or changing equilibrium relationships produces biased forecasts.

assumptions: Joint linear dynamics and exogenous effects are stable and identifiable.
methods.description: Represent multivariate autoregressive-moving-average dynamics with optional exogenous regressors in state space.
failure_conditions: High-dimensional moving-average terms are weakly identified and computationally fragile.

assumptions: Low-dimensional common factors explain most cross-series predictive variation.
methods.description: Extract a small set of latent dynamic factors shared by many observed series and forecast through their state evolution.
failure_conditions: Idiosyncratic dynamics or time-varying loadings defeat the fixed low-rank structure.

assumptions: Smooth long-range history has a compact Legendre and Fourier representation.
methods.description: Project history into Legendre memory coefficients, remove noise through Fourier projection, and forecast with compact frequency-enhanced representations.
failure_conditions: Abrupt transients or irregular sampling are distorted by low-rank spectral compression.

assumptions: A configuration in the searched TBATS family adequately represents the target's trend and seasonal structure.
methods.description: Automatically search TBATS configurations for Box-Cox transformation, ARMA errors, trend damping, and multiple trigonometric seasonalities.
failure_conditions: Short histories or abrupt regime changes make the enlarged automatic search unstable or obsolete.

assumptions: Seasonal phases recur and recent seasonal-naive residuals approximate future uncertainty.
methods.description: Center a forecast on seasonal naive and form a predictive distribution by mixing recency-weighted same-season observations with signed calibration residuals.
failure_conditions: Weak seasonality, thin same-phase history, or a distribution shift makes the empirical pools unrepresentative.

assumptions: Stable dependencies exist both across temporal segments and among observed variables.
methods.description: Embed each variable in temporal segments and alternate cross-time and routed cross-dimension attention in a hierarchical encoder-decoder.
failure_conditions: Weak or shifting cross-variable relationships make the routed dimension attention unnecessary or misleading.

assumptions: Long-horizon structure can be decomposed into trend and recurring patterns visible at a small set of convolution scales.
methods.description: Decompose trend and seasonal components, then use parallel downsampling and isometric convolutions to capture local features and global correlations at multiple scales.
failure_conditions: Irregular events or patterns outside the selected scales are blurred by decomposition and downsampling.

assumptions: Local normalization improves estimation and a compact factor model can restore informative non-stationarity.
methods.description: Stationarize each input series for predictability while injecting learned de-stationary factors into attention and restoring the original output statistics.
failure_conditions: Abrupt or structurally novel distribution shifts cannot be reconstructed from the learned de-stationary factors.

assumptions: Long dependencies are preserved by a hierarchical multi-resolution representation and local cross-scale links.
methods.description: Represent a sequence at multiple resolutions with pyramidal attention links that provide linear complexity and short signal paths for long-range forecasting.
failure_conditions: Important high-frequency details disappear during coarsening or lie outside the fixed pyramidal connectivity.

assumptions: Most predictive information survives complementary interval and contiguous sampling patterns.
methods.description: Apply interval and continuous downsampling to multivariate histories and forecast with lightweight MLP projections over the sampled views.
failure_conditions: Sparse pulses or fine timing relationships lost during downsampling dominate the forecast target.

assumptions: Pretraining patterns transfer to the target frequency and forecast horizon.
methods.description: A patched decoder-only transformer pretrained across heterogeneous series for direct point forecasting.
failure_conditions: Large domain shifts or required context beyond the checkpoint limit reduce zero-shot reliability.

assumptions: Quantized sequence patterns learned from public and synthetic corpora transfer to the target.
methods.description: Scale and quantize values into tokens, then sample continuations from a pretrained T5 language-model family.
failure_conditions: Quantization, unmodeled covariates, and autoregressive sampling can miss sharp conditional events.

assumptions: Cross-frequency and cross-variate patterns in LOTSA transfer to the target variables.
methods.description: A masked encoder universal forecaster using multi-patch-size projections and an any-variate attention design.
failure_conditions: Unseen covariate semantics or data distributions can defeat the universal patch representation.

assumptions: Lag covariates provide a frequency-robust representation transferable across domains.
methods.description: A decoder-only probabilistic forecaster that conditions on lagged values and time features across frequencies.
failure_conditions: Long nonseasonal dependencies and unseen exogenous shocks are poorly represented by fixed lag features.

assumptions: Pretrained representations can be adapted with a small amount of task supervision.
methods.description: A masked-patch encoder pretrained on the Time-series Pile and adapted with task-specific forecasting heads.
failure_conditions: A fixed patch context and weak target-specific adaptation can miss long-horizon dynamics.

assumptions: Resolution-diverse pretraining transfers and a small adaptation head captures target specifics.
methods.description: A compact adaptive-patching mixer pretrained for zero-shot use and lightweight target or covariate adaptation.
failure_conditions: Checkpoint-specific context and horizon pairs constrain direct use on mismatched tasks.

assumptions: Next-patch generative pretraining learns patterns reusable under the target sampling process.
methods.description: A GPT-style model pretrained by next-patch prediction and adapted to forecasting and other generative time-series tasks.
failure_conditions: Channel-independent generation and finite context can miss new cross-variate causal structure.

assumptions: Sparse experts specialize in reusable temporal regimes across large heterogeneous pretraining data.
methods.description: A sparse mixture-of-experts decoder pretrained autoregressively on the Time-300B corpus.
failure_conditions: Unsupported dynamic covariates and context-plus-horizon beyond the trained window limit applicability.

assumptions: The synthetic prior assigns meaningful probability to the target data-generating behavior.
methods.description: A prior-data-fitted network trained on synthetic generators to approximate Bayesian zero-shot forecasting.
failure_conditions: Real dynamics outside the synthetic training prior lead to systematic zero-shot errors.

assumptions: The proprietary pretraining corpus and service adaptation transfer to the submitted target.
methods.description: A hosted pretrained forecasting service supporting zero-shot forecasts, intervals, and exogenous inputs.
failure_conditions: Closed weights and training data limit diagnosis under domain shift or service changes.

assumptions: Prompt and decomposition components align the target distribution with pretrained regimes.
methods.description: A prompt-conditioned pretrained transformer that decomposes trend, seasonality, and residual structure for transfer.
failure_conditions: Incorrect decomposition or a target outside prompt coverage produces negative transfer.

assumptions: A shared sequence-variable representation transfers across tasks and domains with prompting or adaptation.
methods.description: A unified task-tokenized time-series model that supports forecasting, imputation, classification, and anomaly detection.
failure_conditions: Task and domain shifts not represented during pretraining require substantial target-specific tuning.

assumptions: Flow-matching pretraining on TimeBench captures a transferable conditional future distribution.
methods.description: A native continuous-value transformer trained with flow matching to generate multiple future paths.
failure_conditions: Unseen domains or event-conditioned futures absent from numeric context remain underrepresented.

assumptions: Large observability and synthetic pretraining transfers to the target variables and covariates.
methods.description: A multivariate decoder-only probabilistic forecaster scaled for observability and general forecasting data.
failure_conditions: Targets far from observability dynamics or hardware limits for larger checkpoints reduce usefulness.

assumptions: Serial scaling over architecture, data, and training transfers to the target series and horizon.
methods.description: An 8.3B-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts foundation model trained for serial-token time-series prediction with an 11.5K context.
failure_conditions: Numeric history alone cannot resolve unseen event-driven futures or unsupported target semantics.

assumptions: Synthetic multivariate structures teach group attention relationships that transfer to target and covariate groups.
methods.description: A zero-shot universal forecaster using group attention for in-context information sharing among related series, variates, targets, and covariates.
failure_conditions: Unseen group semantics or future events absent from the provided numeric covariates remain unresolved.

assumptions: The 36-million-series corpus and direct quantile objective transfer to the target distribution.
methods.description: A decoder-only single-patch foundation model trained with quantile loss and recursive multi-token prediction.
failure_conditions: Performance declines at long horizons or under domains outside the pretraining corpus.

assumptions: Patch compression and direct multi-step decoding preserve the predictive structure needed for the target horizon.
methods.description: A patch-based Chronos variant whose encoder representations directly produce multi-step quantile forecasts.
failure_conditions: Fixed patch aggregation can miss narrow pulses, while numeric-only input cannot anticipate unobserved events.

assumptions: Sparse experts discover reusable local temporal regimes across heterogeneous pretraining data.
methods.description: A sparse mixture-of-experts universal forecaster that learns token-level specialization instead of routing by a human-defined frequency class.
failure_conditions: Routing can specialize to pretraining regimes that do not represent a new target or an unobserved event-driven future.

assumptions: Temporal dynamics remain expressible after mapping observations into a sampling-rate-invariant coefficient space.
methods.description: A state-space encoder with a continuous functional-basis decoder that adjusts forecasts to the target sampling rate and horizon.
failure_conditions: A poor scale factor or dynamics beyond the learned functional basis degrade long-horizon forecasts.

assumptions: Hierarchical sparse attention learned from a large cross-domain corpus transfers across target scales and sampling patterns.
methods.description: A scalable foundation-model family using hierarchical interleaved block attention to capture local and global temporal dependencies.
failure_conditions: Targets outside the pretraining pattern distribution or requiring unavailable contextual events can defeat zero-shot transfer.

assumptions: Instance-specific token granularity and spectral position scaling transfer across heterogeneous temporal densities.
methods.description: A parameter-efficient zero-shot model with dynamic patching, mixture-of-size encoding, and granularity-aware rotary positions.
failure_conditions: The patch router or spectral scale becomes unreliable for patterns outside the predictability-stratified pretraining corpus.

assumptions: Multiple patch resolutions capture temporal structure that transfers to unseen domains and horizons.
methods.description: An encoder-decoder foundation model that uses multi-resolution patching across real and synthetic pretraining series.
failure_conditions: New temporal scales or contextual events outside the pretraining corpus produce a representation mismatch.

assumptions: Long convolution and recurrent state updates capture transferable dependencies without a large Transformer.
methods.description: A compact hybrid foundation model interleaving long convolutions with linear recurrent DeltaNet layers for efficient zero-shot forecasting.
failure_conditions: Patterns requiring unavailable covariates or poorly represented long-range dynamics defeat the compact recurrent state.

assumptions: Latent prototypes align variable semantics and transferable interactions across multivariate systems.
methods.description: A multivariate foundation model that aligns heterogeneous variables in a prototype space and models positive and negative cross-variate affinity.
failure_conditions: Unseen variable semantics or relationships not expressible by the learned prototype space cause faulty reassembly.

assumptions: Low- and high-energy frequency components plus prompt-routed experts transfer across related domains.
methods.description: A lightweight foundation model combining energy-aware spectral decomposition with a mixture of dataset prompts.
failure_conditions: The prompt router or spectral decomposition misallocates patterns from a novel dataset or abrupt regime.

assumptions: xLSTM state tracking and in-context masking learn transferable short- and long-horizon dynamics.
methods.description: A compact xLSTM foundation model using recurrent state tracking, frequency-aware resampling, and quantile decoding.
failure_conditions: A target outside pretraining domains or an unseen exogenous event cannot be recovered from numeric state alone.

assumptions: A recurrent memory and synthetic multivariate couplings transfer to streaming targets and known-future covariates.
methods.description: A streaming xLSTM foundation model with recurrent univariate state and grouped cross-variate attention for past and future covariates.
failure_conditions: Cross-variate structure outside synthetic coupling patterns or stale streaming state produces persistent errors.

assumptions: Temporal feature engineering converts forecasting into a tabular task covered by TabPFN's synthetic prior.
methods.description: A zero-shot pipeline that transforms temporal history and known-future features into tabular regression for a pretrained TabPFN model.
failure_conditions: Targets needing past-only or static covariate semantics, or lying outside the synthetic tabular prior, are poorly represented.

assumptions: Masked reconstruction over long contexts learns patterns that transfer to unseen target series and forecast masks.
methods.description: A pretrained patch Transformer using masked reconstruction, residual projections, and a dense quantile head for zero-shot forecasting and imputation.
failure_conditions: Context-plus-horizon beyond the fixed window or contextual events absent from numeric history remain unresolved.

assumptions: The updated decoder and long-context pretraining transfer to the target, while supplied future regressors are informative.
methods.description: A 200M-parameter TimesFM release with long context, continuous quantile forecasts, optional external-regressor covariates, and no frequency token.
failure_conditions: Unsupported contextual events, covariate shift, or horizons beyond the configured direct forecast limit degrade predictions.
